title: Flow and decisions: how work moves and how decisions settle

sections.name: claim
sections.label: Claim
sections.content: Work moves through nine stages, each with one trade-off; decisions settle through a flow of their own beside stage 8. Where either stops is recorded as a finding against the stage. The stops, the decisions, the reports and the owner's load were measured together for the first time on 2026-11-03: the flow runs and stops are recorded, but nothing downstream of a stop, a report or a ratification yet changes the practice.

sections.name: story
sections.label: The story so far
sections.content: 2026-10-25: three models of how work moves were written in one day (the archetypal flow with nine stage domains and one trade-off each; model B, made independently; the domain mapped by seven questions) and compared. 2026-10-28: the decision flow was added as a zoom on stage 8 (Arise, Settle by principle, Place, Decide, Record, Cite and revisit), and recording stops as findings was proposed (fbba3d5e, 199dd369) and practised from that day. 2026-10-30: this overview was first written; the trade-offs were untested and the next action was to fill one stage's 2x2 cases with the owner. 2026-11-03: the review found 29 flow stops in six days (Allocate 9, Review and land 7, Build 5), two causes behind half of them (agent PRs collide and go stale; groups sit idle), recurrences filed as new findings instead of counted, and the stage exercises untouched since 10-25. Decisions: form is now filled (rationale 97%, revisit 100% since 10-15) but only 41% argue a case per option, 12% link a precedent, 0 of 110 ratified were ever set aside. Reports: 36 of 37 received, 0 records derived from any; receipt is wired only to the pause rule. The owner: 343 affirmations, 24 sessions at rubber-stamp speed, up to fourteen acts between a story and a buildable issue, the owner step of both end-to-end walks still open after 23 days. The problem domain is already mapped (the relevant problems are affirmed); what is missing is evidence joined to the stages, the 2x2 cases, and remedies that remove the owner from a stage rather than speed the owner up.

sections.name: parts
sections.label: The parts
sections.content:
- The archetypal flow: a fractal map of Programme coordination (2026-10-25): nine stage exercises, each with its trade-off and poles; stops are filed against these.
- Flow model B: an independent model (2026-10-25).
- Programme coordination mapped by seven questions (2026-10-25).
- The decision flow: where decisions go and where they stop (2026-10-28): stage 8 zoomed in; decision stops are filed against its six stages.
- Comparing the flow models (2026-10-25): what the models agree and disagree on; its open question "is Decide a stage or a spine" was answered in practice by the decision flow.
- State of flow, 2026-11-03: a review: the first measured audit (stops, decisions, reports, owner load, tools), with three findings and three exercises beneath it.

sections.name: open
sections.label: What is open
sections.content: Three exercises from the review, in Open exercises: how setting up a domain becomes one affirmation instead of fourteen acts; what gate makes a decision carry a case per option and a precedent search; how a received report becomes a record that changes the practice. By rule, no exercise: fold the duplicate problem pair 31c11d12/c5729f43; give the five problem-less stops a problem; count recurrences on the existing finding; make the handbook's stop table a query over flow-stop findings; map the handbook's 16 steps onto the nine stages once. Still untested: every stage's 2x2 cases. The chartered home for this work is WG Programme practice (clerk#142, decision a8bc55ef).

sections.name: drill
sections.label: How to read it
sections.content: Each part is its own section. Inside the archetypal flow, each stage has its exercise, its trade-off and the two poles with their shadows; the owner's vignettes sit under the exercise they shaped. Stops: srs find --tag flow-stop and --tag decision-stop. The review's findings are tagged flow-review.
